response.mathematical_assessment: The proposed head is well defined for every input with at least one valid token. N_x is an uncentered, attention-weighted second moment of unit state vectors. It is PSD with trace one, so R_x has spectrum in [1/8, 9/8] and condition number at most 9. For unit φ_r, ‖R_x⁻¹φ_r‖ is at least 8/9. The Rayleigh-quotient optimizer and stated gain are correct, with equality exactly when φ_r lies in one eigenspace of R_x. The gain concerns alignment with φ_r relative to the loaded second moment. The classifier instead scores a signed utility average, for which the gain supplies no improvement bound. At fixed parameters the class-0 logit is exactly native. During training, gradients through α_0 and N_x allow positive-relation losses to change φ_0.
known_equivalences: The direction R_x⁻¹φ_r is the standard diagonally loaded adaptive-beamforming direction, here normalized to unit Euclidean norm for a pure Born effect. If N_x is constant across inputs, each resulting direction is a static pure effect, subject to representability by the native effect parameterization.

Hermiticity gives the exact score p_rt = |φ_r† R_x⁻¹ ψ_t|² / (φ_r† R_x⁻² φ_r). This is an equivalent computation on transformed token vectors. With the native EPS, dropping the denominator changes attention in general. In the numerator-only representation the equivalent additive floor is EPS times φ_r† R_x⁻² φ_r.

There is no general absorption into fixed effects for the same prepared token states. For example, take orthogonal states e₀ and e₁, φ_0 = (e₀+e₁)/√2 and φ_r = (e₀−e₁)/√2. With one token of each type, the positive relation gives them equal attention. Duplicating e₀ changes N_x on their span from diag(1/2,1/2) to diag(2/3,1/3). The filtered effect then gives an individual e₀ token less attention than the e₁ token. A fixed native effect cannot change those two individual tokens’ attention ratio when only the multiplicity changes. This argument is conditional on the prepared states and makes no expressivity claim about a retrained encoder.
counterexamples: The full filter can hurt the correct positive relation even when it strictly improves its Rayleigh quotient. Take two tokens |+⟩ = (e₀+e₁)/√2 and |−⟩ = (e₀−e₁)/√2, with φ_0 = |+⟩ and φ_r = e₀. Native positive attention is evenly split. Native α_0 puts more mass on |+⟩, so the full inverse shifts positive attention toward |−⟩. The computational-basis diagonal control leaves e₀ unchanged. Give relation r utilities 1 on |+⟩ and 0 on |−⟩ and hold competing logits constant with zero utilities. For a true-r item, the full arm strictly increases CE against both comparators, including with the specified EPS.

Input dependence alone need not change predictions. If each relation’s utility is constant across valid tokens on an input, every normalized attention gives the same logits there. Also, whenever N_x is diagonal in the declared basis, full and diagonal filtering coincide on that input.
response.causal_limits: Of 478 native errors, 418 cross the class-0 boundary, in both directions. Even a label-aware shared offset can fix at most 12 net errors on these items. That reasonably motivates one test of input-dependent changes to positive evidence. The error counts and pool oracle do not identify which tokens caused the mistakes or establish that α_0 weights nuisance. The mechanism-specific prediction is that using the off-diagonal entries of the α_0-weighted second moment improves CE over diagonal filtering, and that the resulting head also improves over native continuation. Even a pass leaves the nuisance interpretation unresolved because all arms co-adapt during training.
response.nearest_neighbor_limits: Loaded inverse-second-moment filtering, the Rayleigh identity, and input-dependent attention metrics are established ingredients. From the supplied source readings, priority remains unresolved for the specific composition of a native no_relation Born reference, per-input filtering of positive pure effects, and unchanged signed-utility pooling. The full operation is covariant under a common unitary change of state coordinates. Its comparison with the diagonal control measures the value of off-diagonal entries in the chosen computational basis. The supplied Capon metadata does not support an original-text audit.
response.screen_assessment: Use the proposed single 128-update screen on the existing 4192/4000 TRAIN partition. Start all three arms from the same pinned checkpoint and optimizer initialization, use the same batch stream, train all 81,028 head parameters, and score each arm’s update-128 state only after all training finishes. For each comparator, define the paired difference as comparator CE minus full CE. Resample exact-sentence groups together across arms, retaining the item weighting of the reported CE. Require lower full CE against both, a positive 2.5th-percentile bootstrap bound for each difference, and full Macro39 at least as high as both comparators. Report positive-to-zero and zero-to-positive transitions descriptively so a CE pass can be interpreted against its motivating error profile. A miss closes this exact screen. The bootstrap measures assessment-sample sensitivity conditional on these trained arms and this exposed split.
